title: Design: Vendor invoice due date for a shop's Net term
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure vendor invoice A, dated Oct 5, 2026, is saved for a vendor who holds the shop's own term due 10 days after the invoice date.
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide, at 100% zoom.
  • Open the attached design picture ct-p7-11-vendor-on-net-10-oct-5-due-oct-15.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
  • Start on the vendor invoices list (Parts, Vendors, Vendor Invoices).
custom_steps:
1. Open vendor invoice A.
  2. Resize the browser window to 1536 px wide (for example, maximise it on a 1536 x 864 screen at 100% zoom).
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The Vendor Invoice card shows "Invoice date" Oct 5, 2026 and "Due date" Oct 15, 2026 (as in ct-p7-11-vendor-on-net-10-oct-5-due-oct-15.png).

Step 2:

  • At 1536 px nothing overlaps, nothing is cut off and nothing needs a sideways scroll.
  • The layout described above is unchanged, only wider.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11676 (Story 7, Due dates)

  • S7-R1: “A Net term (standard or the shop's own) is due that many days after the invoice date: an invoice dated Oct 5 on Net 30 is due Nov 4; on a shop's "Net 10" it is due Oct 15.”
  • S7-R9: “A vendor invoice stores no term. Its due date is calculated by the same rules from the vendor's term when the vendor invoice is created, recalculated when its invoice date or its vendor changes, and stored.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
